P1.evidence: Setter acknowledged but nothing read back — 'I know you spoke with Kim. He gave me like a little bit of an overview' — with no specifics fed back to make the prospect feel seen. Frame was two-part plus alignment: 'I just want to get a bit of a better idea than what Kim would have got. Get more context... where you're at now, also build out what it is that you actually want and then if there's alignment we'll talk about the coaching.' What's in the way and what you need were both absent. Agreement checked with 'if not that's fine as well, all right?' and open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in this batch so far. Diet and energy both asked directly — 'what's your diet like?' and 'what's your energy levels been like over the last two years?' — and current activity established properly. But age was volunteered in the prospect's opening sentence and never asked, height never asked at all (the rep later said 'Your height and weight's good', implying he was reading the application rather than gathering), and no health-conditions question was ever put: high cholesterol arrived unprompted inside a list of symptoms. Sleep was volunteered inside the energy answer, not asked. The injury question was approached obliquely through 'What have you seen differently... it's been two years?', which did establish duration but never asked directly about injuries or movement limitations, so the longstanding lower back weakness surfaced only later and by accident.

P3.evidence: The reflect-back was the best moment of the call and landed cleanly: 'It doesn't sound like what you're bothered about is like, oh, I look worse. It's more about like, my quality of life's lower... I'm not as capable, I guess would be a good word' — confirmed with 'Yeah, just not capable of doing certain things.' Six-month success question ran, and mobility, strength and energy were all separated out. But the bridge question was never asked, and the identity and longevity material was entirely prospect-generated: he supplied 'you see people struggling, not walking properly, can't climb up stairs... you think to yourself, ah, it's never gonna happen to me' with no prompting. Critically, 'who else does that impact?' was never asked. He is married, the wife is the reason the sale did not close, and she was not mentioned once before the price.

P4.evidence: The gap was elicited well by offering a menu — 'some people, it's like, I need the accountability, some people it's more so the structure and just the knowledge. What do you feel like is important for you?' — and the prospect named it precisely: 'the accountability is a big thing for me, if there's no one holding me accountable, I'll just do nothing, so, terrible.' Past attempts were only half-covered: the abandoned JD Gym membership came up but was never interrogated beyond 'it's not my thing', and neither 'why do you feel it didn't stick' nor 'what's the one thing actually getting in the way' was asked. The real structural barrier — everything he owns, including his bikes, sitting in storage for two years — was volunteered and never explored as the blocker it plainly is.

P5.evidence: Never ran, and this is the most expensive omission on the call because the prospect built the frame himself and handed it over: 'I would imagine another year of this and there's no turning around', and earlier, 'by doing nothing, I'm aging a lot faster than I should have.' Not one follow-up was asked — no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. When the wife objection arrived twenty minutes later the rep had no emotional leverage in hand and went straight to a deposit.

P6.evidence: No commitment check ran. Belief was never tested — 'do you believe you can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in your corner' was not asked in any form. Nor was the all-in question, which is the specific move that surfaces a spouse before the price rather than after it. What the rep took as commitment was philosophical alignment and an absence of questions: 'does that align with you in terms of philosophy?' — 'it certainly does', and 'any questions on the process? Anything that doesn't make sense?' — 'No, it sounds basically like what I'm looking for.' That is agreement with a description, not a yes to going all in.

P11.evidence: The checkout was shared on screen and walked through, but what was actually processed was the $100 refundable deposit, not the programme fee. No onboarding call with Trevor was booked — Monday or Tuesday were floated in the abstract and left there. No agreement email and nothing signed. Partial credit on the last step only because the rep described the onboarding form and promised pre-call access to the informational material; no welcome email, no Skool community link, and the questionnaire was described rather than sent.

objection_plays.detail: The clearest OB trigger in the batch — 'I have to discuss with my wife' and 'do you mind if I just have a conversation with my wife and then reach out to you on Monday?' The rep ran exactly one move from the play, and it was the last-resort fallback: put down a deposit, go talk to her, full refund if she says no. Every diagnostic move ahead of it was skipped — no 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal', no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain', no 'is this genuinely needing her input, or asking permission to bet on yourself', and no 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house.' Jumping straight to the fallback converted a live objection into a rescheduled call and a refundable $100.

'So I'll think about it' was said in the same breath as the wife objection. No OA move ran at all — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is.' The rep's immediate reply was to concede: 'That's absolutely fine. If I told you, no, I'd be an [expletive], right?'

A soft money signal was present — 'I think that's doable. I'll have to double check the finances.' No isolation, no financial picture, none of it. More notable is the sequencing: the rep volunteered the payment split before any objection existed, immediately after naming the price — 'If needs be, we can always break it up as well. We don't want money to be the reason why you don't get the results you want.' Offering the concession before the resistance removes the play's entire purpose.

notes: Genuinely good discovery and the best reflect-back in the batch, then the two phases that create commitment — P5 and P6 — were skipped entirely, so a warm, well-qualified, well-funded 57-year-old who described the programme as 'basically what I'm looking for' left without buying. Two concrete coaching points: ask 'who else does that impact' on any married prospect so the spouse is in the room before the price, not after it; and stop offering to break up the payment before anyone has objected to it.
